children: WINNIPEG, Manitoba--ICE canola futures were weaker Tuesday morning, taking back some of Monday's gains as speculators took profits on their large long positions.
The November contract was down 5.60 Canadian dollars at C$829.60 per ton in early activity.
Losses in the Chicago soy complex added to the softer tone, with crude oil, European rapeseed and Malaysian palm oil also lower on the day.
Warm and dry Prairie weather forecasts should allow farmers to make good harvest progress over the next week.
The Canadian dollar was weaker relative to its United States counterpart in early activity, which underpins crush margins and makes exports more attractive for international buyers.
About 15,500 canola contracts had traded as of 9:38 a.m. ET.
